info.description: API documentation for Product Management Service

bearerAuth.description: API key authorization. Pass your API key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Both new (`gsk_*`) and legacy (`gsk-`) API keys are accepted, e.g. `Authorization: Bearer gsk_...` or `Authorization: Bearer gsk-...`.

input.description: Structured input data. For plain text input, format is { user_message: "..." }. Uploaded files ride a `content` array of parts, each `{ type: "file", uri, filename, mimeType }`, beside an optional `user_message`. A file part is a Galtea file when its uri names a Galtea storage key (`files/<organization>/<32 hex>.<extension>`); every other element is stored as sent. For a Galtea file, `mimeType` is filled from the stored object when omitted, and `filename` is filled only where the storage records it: AWS does, Azure Blob does not, so send `filename` on an Azure deployment. Every Galtea file part is returned with a server-measured `sizeBytes`; a value sent for it is ignored.

context.description: Structured context data. For plain text context, format is { value: "..." }

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language tag (e.g. en, es-MX). The region subtag selects the regional variety in simulated user messages and voice synthesis; generated test text keeps the base language. The value is stored as the full tag. A bare code for ca, de, es, eu, fr, gl, it, nl or pt defaults to the European variety of that language, in simulated user messages only (pt -> pt-PT); an explicit region always overrides it, and neither voice synthesis nor the stored value is affected.

gender.description: Persona-derived gender ("MALE"/"FEMALE") for the male/female synthesized caller voice in phone (voice) evaluations. A voice pinned for the call's locale takes precedence. Ignored by text evaluations.

backgroundNoiseProfile.description: Background noise mixed into the simulated caller audio during a voice test. Clip-backed (office, street, car) or synthetic (white, pink). Null means off; set together with backgroundNoiseLevel.

backgroundNoiseLevel.description: How loud the background noise is relative to the caller speech. Null means off; set together with backgroundNoiseProfile.

testCaseGroupId.description: Revision family key shared by every revision of this test case.

parentTestCaseId.description: The revision this row was forked from; null for a family root.

legacyAt.description: Set when this revision was superseded by a newer one; null for the active head.

conversationHistory.description: Predefined conversation for this SCENARIOS test case. The API stores it as a seed session and returns that session id in seedSessionId. Write-only: the array itself is never echoed back, read the predefined conversation through the seed session. Sending it again replaces the predefined conversation; an identical array changes nothing. Omit the field to leave the predefined conversation untouched; null is rejected. Cannot be sent together with seedSessionId, which is the other way to give this test case a conversation.

content.example: I want to open an account

seedSessionId.description: Read and write mean different things here, and the two ids are never the same session. On a response it is the seed session holding this test case predefined conversation, or null when it has none. On a request it is the SOURCE session to copy, which must be a session of this test product. The API answers with the id of the copy it made, never with the id you sent. Omit it, send null, or send back the id the response gave you, and the predefined conversation stays as it is. There is no way to remove a predefined conversation. Cannot be sent together with conversationHistory, the other way to give this test case a conversation.

CompatibleMetric.description: Metric annotated with compatibility against the evaluation context: product metadata, test-case availability, and the conversation endpoint connection output mapping when the evaluation has to produce new output. Span-dependent and runtime-only params are out of scope and treated as always satisfied.

source.description: Evaluation method for the metric. `FULL_PROMPT` is deprecated for creation — `POST /metrics` rejects it with a 400. Use `PARTIAL_PROMPT` for new AI Evaluation metrics. The value remains in the enum because existing FULL_PROMPT metrics are still returned by reads and filters.

isCompatible.description: Whether the metric can be satisfied by the resolved evaluation context. Always checked against the product metadata and test-case availability; the conversation endpoint connection output mapping is only checked when the evaluation has to produce new output. For a session, a metric is also incompatible when a file on a side it reads is one its judge would not read (`conversation_turns` reads both sides), or when it reads `input`, no turn yields text and audio on a turn has no transcript, unless the input side carries a file or no judge scores the metric (human evaluation, self-hosted). Pass `inferenceResultId` to answer for the one turn a run would judge.

incompatibilityReason.description: Human-readable explanation of why the metric is incompatible. Non-null iff `isCompatible === false`.

relevance.description: How relevant the metric is to the tests the evaluation runs against. `linked`: linked to a specification of one of those tests. `matching`: linked to a same-product specification whose testType matches one of those tests. `none`: neither, or no test context was provided.

AnalyticsInsightFlag.description: A single deterministic red flag / proactive insight computed over the analytics aggregation. Contextual fields are populated only when they apply to the flag type.

description.example: Faithfulness scored 42% on v3; 12 of 78 evaluations scored zero (15.4%).

failureRate.description: Percentage (0-100) of the metric's scored evaluations that scored exactly zero within the request filters; null when the stats were unavailable.

evaluationCount.description: Scored evaluations behind failureRate; null when the stats were unavailable.

AnalyticsInsights.description: Single-version analytics insights: deterministic flags plus a fail-open LLM-generated narrative summary (the narrative is omitted when the request sets `includeNarrative=false`).

narrative.description: LLM-generated narrative summary, or null when generation was skipped (`includeNarrative=false` or no flags) or failed.
narrative.example: Faithfulness dropped sharply on v3 and two specifications still have no coverage.

narrativeGeneratedByAi.description: True when the narrative was successfully produced by the LLM; false otherwise (including when `includeNarrative=false`).

AnalyticsInsightsComparison.description: Cross-version analytics comparison insights: deterministic flags plus a fail-open LLM-generated narrative summary (the narrative is omitted when the request sets `includeNarrative=false`).

narrative.description: LLM-generated narrative summary, or null when generation was skipped (`includeNarrative=false` or no flags) or failed.
narrative.example: Faithfulness regressed from v2 to v3 while latency on v3 is 1.6× the cheapest version.

narrativeGeneratedByAi.description: True when the narrative was successfully produced by the LLM; false otherwise (including when `includeNarrative=false`).

SessionInput.description: Session creation input. `versionId` is optional: when omitted, provide `productId` and the API reuses the product's latest version (creating a default first version if the product has none). One of `versionId` or `productId` is required. `testCaseId` and `isProduction` are independent: a session can be production (no testCaseId), test-driven non-production (testCaseId set, isProduction defaults to false), or externally-ingested non-production (no testCaseId, isProduction explicitly false — typical for imported traces). The only forbidden combination is `testCaseId` set together with `isProduction=true`. When `testCaseId` is set, `context` is rejected because it would be derived from the test case.

versionId.description: Version ID to create the session for. Optional when productId is provided; one of versionId or productId is required.

productId.description: Product to anchor the session when versionId is omitted. The API reuses the product's latest version or creates a default one. Ignored when versionId is provided.

customId.description: Optional caller-defined identifier for the session

testCaseId.description: Test case to link this session to. Forbidden when isProduction=true. Defaults to omitted, in which case isProduction defaults to true.

isProduction.description: Whether the session represents real production traffic. Defaults to true when testCaseId is omitted and false when testCaseId is set. May be set explicitly to false without a testCaseId for externally-ingested sessions (e.g. trace imports).

context.description: Additional context for the session. Accepts a plain string or a structured JSON object. Forbidden when testCaseId is set (the context is derived from the test case).

status.description: Initial session status. Defaults to PENDING (open, accepts new turns); the session closes on an explicit finish or the product auto-close sweep (#3384).

runId.description: Run to attribute this session to, so several sessions a client creates are grouped together. It must name a run you opened with POST /runs: a run a platform launch opened settles with that launch and is rejected here, as is a deleted, finished, other-product or other-version run. Forbidden when isProduction is true.

InferenceResult.description: A trace: one conversation turn, holding the input and the agent output. The schema name, the `/inferenceResults` path and every `inferenceResult*` field still carry the old name of this entity, "inference result". Only the wording changed so far; the wire contract is renamed in a later API release.

error.description: Error message explaining why this trace failed or was skipped

input.description: Structured input data. For plain text input, format is { user_message: "..." }. A `content` array of parts (audio or file) can sit beside an optional `user_message`. Each element of a `content` array is read on its own. A file part is a Galtea file when its uri names a Galtea storage key (`files/<organization>/<32 hex>.<extension>`, on any host): it is stored signature-free and checked as on a test case input (at most 20 files and 20 MB, an accepted file type, a file of this organization), otherwise 400. A Galtea file missing from storage is stored signature-free without its sizeBytes, and every other element as sent. With `INLINE_MEDIA_COPY_ENABLED` on, a binary file of 1,024 base64 characters or more, held in a data URI or in the byte field of a provider object, is stored as a Galtea file token instead. A metric scores a Galtea file only when its judge model reads that kind of file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or PDF); any other metric that reads this side is skipped, except a human evaluation or self-hosted one, and the reason names the file.

actualOutput.description: The agent turn output. Plain text by default (the scored scalar). An envelope { assistant_message, content: [...] } carries a `content` array of parts (audio or file) beside an optional `assistant_message` — the scored scalar stays the canonical transcript, and an answer that is only a file carries no scalar at all. A metric scores a Galtea file only when its judge model reads that kind of file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or PDF); any other metric that reads this side is skipped, except a human evaluation or self-hosted one, and the reason names the file.

droppedSpanCount.description: How many spans sent with this trace were refused, for example a span with an empty name or a negative latency. Null means none were refused.

endUser.description: The end user of this trace, set by OTel ingest from its own spans. Read-only. The session holds the first end user of all its traces.

traceId.description: W3C trace ID Galtea sends in the `traceparent` header on this Direct Inference turn. Stored when the turn starts. This is the OpenTelemetry trace id, not the id of this Galtea trace, which is `id`.

comments.description: Free-form reviewer annotations on this turn, oldest first.

Trace.description: A span: one step inside a trace, such as a tool call, a retrieval or an LLM call. The schema name and the `/traces` path still carry the old name of this entity, "trace". The parent trace is `inferenceResultId`; the `parentTraceId` field is the parent span, not the trace. Span ids start with `trace_`, so a `trace_` id belongs here and never to a trace.

description.example: Fetches user data from the database by ID
description.description: Human-readable description of the operation. Maximum 1MB.

inputData.description: Input parameters passed to the operation

outputData.description: Result returned by the operation. Usually an object; a plain string for retrieval-context spans

parentTraceId.description: ID of parent span for hierarchical relationships

modelId.description: The model that answered this LLM call, matched by name when the span was ingested. Null when no live model of the organization, or global model, had any of the model names of the span. A name also matches without its provider prefix. Deleting the model keeps it, so it can name a deleted model.

modelName.description: The model name the span reported, whether or not it matched a model.

inputTokens.description: Input tokens the LLM call reported, cached input included. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

outputTokens.description: Output tokens the LLM call reported. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

cacheReadInputTokens.description: Input tokens the LLM call read from the cache, a part of `inputTokens` priced at the cache-read rate. A count above `inputTokens` is taken as counted apart and flagged in the metadata. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

tokens.description: Sum of the input and output tokens, so cached input counts once, plus the cache read when the source counted it apart from the input. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

costPerInputToken.description: Price of one input token, frozen at ingest from the model of this call, or from the version model when the span names no model. Null when the named model links to nothing or has no price. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

costPerOutputToken.description: Price of one output token, frozen at ingest like costPerInputToken. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

costPerCacheReadInputToken.description: Price of one cache-read token, frozen at ingest like costPerInputToken. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

cost.description: Cost of this call at the frozen rates. Null when no rates were found. A turn's cost sums its spans' costs. Null without `evaluation.readInference` on the product.

RejectedSpan.description: One span a batch create refused. Its siblings were still created.

index.description: Position of the span in the request array, so the caller can find it.

name.description: Name the span was sent with. Null when it carried no usable name.

CreateSpansBatchResult.description: Batch create result returned when `includeRejected=true`. `partialSuccess` is present only when at least one span was refused.

testVariant.description: Only applicable for POLICY specifications. QUALITY: rag, entity_extraction, summarization, classification, translation, correction, other. RED_TEAMING: data_leakage, financial_attacks, illegal_activities, misuse, toxicity, custom.

isCritical.description: Marks a specification whose failure is serious for the business. Defaults to false. Must not be true for INABILITY specifications.

status.description: new = a fresh addition. updated = refines/extends an existing specification. contradictory = conflicts with an existing specification.

jobId.description: Id of the BullMQ job processing the import. Poll `GET /jobs/{jobId}/status` for state.

versionId.description: Id of the Version the imported sessions will belong to: the versionId sent in the request, or the version resolved from productId (issue #3011).

phoneNumber.description: The phone number Galtea dials, in E.164 format.

agentSpeaksFirst.description: Whether the voice agent opens the conversation once the call connects. `false` (default) means the simulated caller speaks first; `true` suits interviewer-style agents that greet first.

apiKey.description: Pipecat Cloud PUBLIC API key (`pk_...`) Galtea uses to provision a room via the runtime `/start` call. This is NOT the `pcc_pat_` Personal Access Token used to deploy agents. MonitorScorePoint.description: Sampling-weighted score over a set of scored sessions. Below 30 scored sessions confidenceInterval is null and collectingData is true; score stays the point estimate (null only when nothing scored).

confidenceInterval.description: 95% confidence interval, present only at 30 or more scored sessions.

MonitorResults.description: Aggregated results for a monitor over a trailing window, computed only from the monitor's own evaluations.

metrics.description: One score series per metric family the monitor scores.

worstMetric.description: Lowest-scoring metric family over the range. Never an average across metrics.

samplingChanges.description: Effective sampling rate over the range. The FIRST element is the baseline (the rate already in effect when the range opens), not a change; every later element is a real change. Skip the first when drawing "sampling changed" markers.

spend.description: The spent and pending credits are null when the caller may not read inference costs on the product of the monitor: a product-scoped role needs a group that lists `evaluation.readInference` there.

waiting.description: Production sessions attached to the monitor not yet closed (capped at 100).

ParseCurlEndpointConnectionResult.description: Result of parsing a raw cURL command. `parsed` is best-effort and always present (even when `errors` is non-empty); `errors` lists structured reasons the command could not be fully parsed.

authToken.description: Bearer token or API key extracted from the command (when present).

inputTemplate.description: Best-effort Jinja2 input template derived from a JSON body. Null when the body is absent or not JSON.

inputTemplateGeneratedByAi.description: True when `inputTemplate` was produced by the LLM enrichment pass (placing the full placeholder vocabulary) rather than the deterministic single-leaf heuristic. Lets the caller badge the field as AI-generated vs auto-filled.

name.description: Suggested connection name. A deterministic host-based default (`{host} {Type} Connection`) for every type, upgraded by the LLM enrichment pass for CONVERSATION using the URL and the optional `productName`.

nameGeneratedByAi.description: True when `name` was produced by the LLM enrichment pass rather than the deterministic host-based floor. Lets the caller badge the field as AI-generated vs auto-filled.

On a create, a modelId you send is the model; when you omit it or send null or an empty string, a model fact links the model (see facts). On an update, a model fact links the model only when you omit modelId and the version has no model; null clears the model.

facts.description: The agent state this version represents, as a flat map of text to text. Every key and every value is trimmed, an entry whose key or value is then empty is dropped, and the rest is kept exactly, so "0.7" and "0.70" are two different facts. At most 32 keys, and at most 2000 bytes once the map is encoded as JSON, which counts its punctuation too. No key and no value may hold the NUL character or half of a surrogate pair. Two keys that become equal after the spaces around them are removed are refused, unless both become empty, which drops them instead because a blank key names no fact; a key repeated with the exact same spelling never reaches that rule, because JSON parsing keeps only its last value. Two live versions of one product may not hold the same facts; the key order you send does not change that comparison. A map that leaves no entry is stored as null. A fact whose key is "model" or "model_name" (case, "_" and "-" are ignored, so "modelName" counts too) is a model fact. It can link the version to the model whose name equals its value, provider prefix included (for example "azure/gpt-4o") and ignoring case. The model must be one the product organization can use: one of its own models or a global one. Its own model wins over a global model of the same name. Model facts that find two different models link none.

otelInputSourceRule.description: Recover a turn's user-visible input for products whose user message lives on a non-LLM span. Set per organization, product or version. Per turn the value it extracts IS the turn input, ahead of every fallback, and the turn input is EMPTY when the rule extracts nothing from any span of the turn. The two directions resolve independently.

otelOutputSourceRule.description: Recover a turn's user-visible output for templated or non-LLM replies whose final answer lives on a non-LLM span. Set per organization, product or version. The version rule wins, then the product rule. Per span it applies only when no LLM output is present. Per turn the value it extracts IS the turn output, ahead of every fallback, and the turn output is EMPTY when the rule extracts nothing from any span of the turn. The two directions resolve independently.

productId.description: Product the version belongs to.

facts.description: The agent state this version represents, as a flat map of text to text. Every key and every value is trimmed, an entry whose key or value is then empty is dropped, and the rest is kept exactly, so "0.7" and "0.70" are two different facts. At most 32 keys, and at most 2000 bytes once the map is encoded as JSON, which counts its punctuation too. No key and no value may hold the NUL character or half of a surrogate pair. Two keys that become equal after the spaces around them are removed are refused, unless both become empty, which drops them instead because a blank key names no fact; a key repeated with the exact same spelling never reaches that rule, because JSON parsing keeps only its last value. Two live versions of one product may not hold the same facts; the key order you send does not change that comparison. A map that leaves no entry is stored as null. A fact whose key is "model" or "model_name" (case, "_" and "-" are ignored, so "modelName" counts too) is a model fact. It can link the version to the model whose name equals its value, provider prefix included (for example "azure/gpt-4o") and ignoring case. The model must be one the product organization can use: one of its own models or a global one. Its own model wins over a global model of the same name. Model facts that find two different models link none. At least one key and value must survive the trimming, or the call is refused. A version this call creates is linked to the model a model fact names; a version it finds keeps its model.

post.description:
Two modes, selected by the request body:

- **Spec mode** (provide `specificationIds`): generates 1-3 metric configurations per
  specification, optionally creating the metrics automatically.
- **Completion mode** ("Complete With AI", provide `name` + `description` + `evaluationType`):
  completes a single metric the user is authoring. The name/description/evaluationType/tags
  are the source of truth; only the judge prompt and evaluation params are generated (for
  CLASSIFIER, config[0] is { classifierQuestion, evaluationParams, conditions, refused }
  instead). `specificationIds` may carry at most one id as optional context.

The evaluator model of every generated AI-evaluated metric is the deployment's setting for
generated metrics, not a choice of the generator. It answers 500 when that model is not
selectable in the environment. A CLASSIFIER result carries no model.

See [Metrics](https://docs.galtea.ai/concepts/metric).

Retrieve the status of an async job (e.g., inference generation). Returns the job state, progress, result, and any error information.

Tenant isolation: a job is only visible to users in the same organization as the user who dispatched it.
Cross-tenant reads receive `404` (rather than `403`) to avoid leaking the existence of jobs in other organizations.
System jobs (those without an owning user) are never exposed through this endpoint.

parameters.description: The ID of the job to check

The current state of the job. `cancelled` is surfaced once the user
calls `POST /jobs/{jobId}/cancel`; it is distinct from `failed`,
which is reserved for unintentional errors. `unknown` is what the queue answers
when it cannot classify the job, for example one removed mid-call.

post.description:
Cancel a queued or in-flight async job (e.g., inference generation). Use this to
stop a doomed batch instead of waiting for every unit to fail individually.

Behaviour:
- A queued or delayed job is removed from the queue and will never run.
- An in-flight job receives a cooperative-cancellation signal: the worker
  observes it at its next checkpoint and stops dispatching further work
  (for inference generation, this means no further sessions are created).
  Work already in progress when the signal is observed is NOT rolled back —
  sessions that have already been created remain. Subsequent reads of
  `GET /jobs/{jobId}/status` will surface the distinct `cancelled` state.
- The in-flight guarantee applies only to handlers that implement the
  cooperative-cancellation checkpoint. Today that is inference generation;
  other job types (e.g. trace imports) do not yet observe the cancel signal
  and will run to completion even though the cancel call returns 200 and the
  status read flips to `cancelled`. Trace imports are short, so this is a
  deliberate Phase-1 trade-off rather than a correctness issue.

Tenant isolation: only users in the dispatching user's organization may
cancel a job. Cross-tenant cancels return `404` (not `403`) to avoid leaking
the existence of jobs in other organizations — matching `GET /jobs/{jobId}/status`.

parameters.description: The ID of the job to cancel

409.description: The job is already in a terminal state (`completed` or `failed`) and cannot be cancelled.

get.summary: Get human annotation count and optimization eligibility
get.description:
Returns the optimization-eligibility snapshot for a metric.

`count` is the number of evaluations that have both an AI score and a human-provided score (annotation). For FULL_PROMPT/PARTIAL_PROMPT metrics this means the AI judged the evaluation and a human later reviewed it. For HUMAN_EVALUATION metrics both fields hold the same human-provided value (for analytics compatibility).

`disagreementCount` is the subset of `count` where the human verdict flips the AI's verdict. Both are binarized at the metric's pass threshold (a score at or above it is class 1, anything below is class 0) and the row counts only when the two classes differ. These are the rows the optimizer learns from.

`minAnnotations` and `minDisagreements` are the api-enforced thresholds (mirrored from the metrics-generator hard thresholds). Optimize is rejected early unless `count >= minAnnotations` AND `disagreementCount >= minDisagreements`.

`plannedSplit` is the split the next optimize would make, from the same count gates and split the run applies: the training and validation row counts, or the refusal text when optimize would answer a 400 (too few annotations, too few disagreements, or too few left to train on after the evaluations earlier attempts kept for validation).

A caller limited to the products its user groups grant gets counts and a split from the evaluations of those products only.

post.description: Starts an optimization run that sends the metric's human-annotated evaluations to the metrics-generator service, which uses the gap between AI and human scores to produce a candidate judge prompt. Only PARTIAL_PROMPT metrics owned by an organization can be optimized, and the source must be its family's active revision with no candidate already awaiting review. Rejected with 400 unless the metric has at least `minAnnotations` evaluations annotated by a human AND `minDisagreements` of those disagree with the AI score. A caller limited to the products its user groups grant sends, and counts, the evaluations of those products only; both thresholds are returned by `GET /metrics/{id}/human-annotation-count` (defaults `10` and `5`, configurable via the `OPTIMIZE_MIN_ANNOTATIONS_HARD` / `OPTIMIZE_MIN_DISAGREEMENTS_HARD` env vars). From 30 annotated evaluations the run holds out a validation set (one third of them, at least 10, chosen by session) that the optimizer only scores after its search and never searches on. Sessions kept from earlier attempts of the metric stay held out. The split, and the validation results once the run finishes, are on `optimizationValidation` of the metric. The caller needs `metric.create` and `metric.update` on the source, since applying or declining the candidate needs `metric.update`. Returns a placeholder metric with isBeingOptimized=true; once the run finishes, the source is untouched and the result is a candidate to review with `POST /metrics/{id}/activate-optimization` or `POST /metrics/{id}/decline-optimization`. See [Metrics](https://docs.galtea.ai/concepts/metric).
